title: The City That Paid For More Rats
sources: Wikipedia, 'Great Hanoi Rat Massacre' (1902 bounty: one cent per rat, proof by tail; rats seen without tails)
Atlas Obscura, 'Hanoi Rat Massacre 1902' (new sewers = rat paradise; bounty scrapped)
Saigoneer, Michael Vann on Hanoi's colonial rat hunt (hunters cutting tails and releasing rats; archive tallies)
Culture Trip, 'The Story Behind Hanoi's Rat Massacre of 1902' (rat farming reported)

lines.text: the rats have no tails, and the city is paying for it.
Hanoi, nineteen oh two. A fancy new sewer opens, and rats move in by the thousands.
An official slams the desk. "Pay everyone for every dead rat!"
"One cent each. Bring the tail as proof."
By morning, hunters line up with buckets full of tails.
"Thousands of rats, gone!" he cheers. "The plan is working!"
Then an inspector climbs down into the sewer, and a rat sprints past him.
"Wait. Why does that rat have no tail?"
Hunters were cutting off the tails, and letting the rats run free.
"Why kill the rat that lays your paycheck?"
Picture paying a gardener for every weed he pulls.
Very soon, that gardener is planting weeds.
Reports say some people even started breeding rats, just to cash in.
The official stares at the bucket. "We paid them to make more rats."
The bounty failed, and the rats kept winning.
